name: question-reproduce-first
prompt: why does test_board_half_rounds_up_even in test_gauge.py fail? the sibling test with 101/102 passes and I don't get it
checks: python:from gauge import board_level as b; assert b([100, 101]) == 100, 'code changed'
assertions: Reproduces first: runs the failing test (or the code) and reads the real result before explaining anything
States the problem as a hypothesis that one named result could show false, with no cause or fix built into it, and only afterwards gives the cause it found as evidence

Answers correctly: board_level uses Python's round(), which rounds an exact half to the nearest even number (banker's rounding). The mean 100.5 goes to 100 and 101.5 goes to 102, so the two tests differ. It is not a float error, not the clean() filter, and not a bug in the mean
